results:
The study you're asking about is Hall et al. (2019) in *Cell Metabolism*, and the search results confirm its core details. It was published May 16, 2019 (DOI 10.1016/j.cmet.2019.05.008).

- **Design:** The NIH team admitted 20 weight-stable adults and randomized them to ultra-processed or unprocessed diets. Each diet ran two weeks, then the groups switched. The participants had a mean age of 31.2 years and a BMI of 27 kg/m2.
- **Matching:** Meals were designed to match on presented calories, energy density, macronutrients, sugar, sodium, and fiber. Participants could eat as much or as little as they wanted.
- **Main result:** Intake rose by about 508 kcal/day on the ultra-processed diet. The extra calories came mostly from carbohydrate and fat, with no meaningful change in protein. Weight gain occurred on the ultra-processed diet despite the matching. Weight loss occurred on the unprocessed diet.
- **Caveats:** Investigators acknowledged that the food was prepared for participants, so convenience and cost were not captured. The study was not designed or powered to test whether particular macronutrients altered intake apart from their caloric content. Hall has also said that lower-income people may face real barriers to preparing unprocessed meals.

The search returned abstracts, press coverage, and secondary commentary, but not the full paper, so the figures above come from the abstract and summaries.

content.text:
**答案：Kevin D. Hall。** 他是美国国立卫生研究院（NIH）下属 NIDDK 的研究员。

这项试验是 Hall 等人 2019 年 5 月发表在 *Cell Metabolism* 上的论文《Ultra-Processed Diets Cause Excess Calorie Intake and Weight Gain》（DOI: 10.1016/j.cmet.2019.05.008）。研究让 20 名成年人住院，交叉轮换吃超加工饮食和未加工饮食，每种各两周，可以随意吃。结果是吃超加工饮食时每天多摄入约 508 千卡。

这个问题我只搜了 1 次。搜到的是期刊抄录的论文 PDF、新闻报道和评论，没有打开期刊官网的原文页面。

来源：
- [Kevin Hall Ultraprocessed Cell Metab 19（论文 PDF）](https://www.foodpolitics.com/wp-content/uploads/Kevin-Hall_Ultraprocessed_Cell-Metab_19.pdf)

- [Natural Medicine Journal: Ultra processed food consumption, appetite and weight gain](https://www.naturalmedicinejournal.com/journal/ultra-processed-food-consumption-appetite-and-weight-gain)
